paper_role: Paper 2 empirical generality lane; not yet part of the canonical claim stack
question: Does phenological responsiveness weaken when organisms must act using information farther removed from the future ecological state they need to match?
design_principle: Keep inferential contrasts within source datasets. Use pollinator-versus-migrant contrasts as cross-system triangulation, not as a causal taxon comparison.

sources.citation: Freimuth J, Bossdorf O, Scheepens JF, Willems FM. 2022. Climate warming changes synchrony of plants and pollinators. Proceedings of the Royal Society B 289:20212142.
sources.published_scope: Germany, 1980-2020; 1764 species total including 20 bee, 22 fly, 206 butterfly/moth and 77 beetle species plus 1438 plants

archive_semantics.rnd_eff_temp_slope: species random-slope deviation from the taxonomic-group mixed model, not the total species temperature slope
archive_semantics.rnd_eff_temp_slope_std_err: standard error of the random-slope estimate
archive_semantics.total_species_slope_rule: do not use the archived random slope as a total species slope; total slope requires the appropriate group fixed temperature coefficient plus the species random-slope deviation
archive_semantics.group_reconstruction_requirement: taxonomic-group membership and group fixed temperature coefficients must be source-backed before any total species-slope distribution is reported

sources.citation: Usui T, Butchart SHM, Phillimore AB. 2017. Temporal shifts and temperature sensitivity of avian spring migratory phenology: a phylogenetic meta-analysis. Journal of Animal Ecology 86:250-261.

primary_analysis.response: temperature slope in days per degree C with its reported standard error
primary_analysis.moderator: population migration distance class as coded by the source study
primary_analysis.contrast: short-distance minus long-distance migrant temperature responsiveness
primary_analysis.directional_prediction: short-distance migrants show more negative temperature slopes than long-distance migrants
primary_analysis.interpretation: replication/benchmark for spatial information-distance, not a novel effect and not proof that cue distance is the causal mechanism

reconstruction_model.effect_size: reported slope in days per degree C
reconstruction_model.primary_moderator: source-coded short- versus long-distance migration class
reconstruction_model.dependence: retain repeated species/study/location structure; at minimum use a multilevel meta-regression with source identifiers and a study-level robust sensitivity
reconstruction_model.phylogeny_boundary: the source paper's published result used Bayesian phylogenetic meta-analysis across 100 trees; a reconstruction without those trees is a dependence-aware robustness analysis, not an exact reproduction of the published phylogenetic model

secondary_benchmark.response: archived species random-slope deviation for temperature plus source-backed taxonomic-group fixed temperature effect when reconstructable
secondary_benchmark.use: audit local phenological temperature-response heterogeneity; published group-level fixed-effect slopes remain external anchors unless the exact fixed coefficients and group mapping are source-reconstructed
secondary_benchmark.cross_source_inference: descriptive triangulation only; no pooled pollinator-versus-bird causal coefficient
secondary_benchmark.random_effect_warning: rnd_eff_temp.csv slope is a random-effect deviation and must never be reported directly as the species total days-per-degree-C response

hard_boundaries: Do not fit a single pollinator-versus-bird coefficient and interpret it causally; source study, taxon, geography and phenophase are confounded.
Do not call the cross-system comparison a new meta-analysis until raw effect-size rows, variances, dependence structure and eligibility are reconstructed.
Do not use published aggregate values as if they were independent effect-size rows.
Do not claim that local pollinators universally track climate better than migrants.
Do not alter the canonical Paper 2 manuscript until the raw-source reconstruction and declared analyses are complete.
Do not treat Freimuth rnd_eff_temp.csv random slopes as total species temperature slopes; they are deviations around source-model fixed effects.
Do not describe a non-phylogenetic Usui reconstruction as an exact reproduction of the original 100-tree MCMCglmm analysis.
promotion_gate: R0 source identity recorded for both datasets
R1 raw bytes acquired and checksums pinned
R2 schema, units and random-effect semantics reproduced
R3 published source-level anchor values and data dimensions cross-checked within declared tolerance
R4 Usui temperature-effect rows rerun with dependence-aware uncertainty; any omission of phylogeny is explicit
R5 Freimuth benchmark reports group fixed-effect anchors separately from species random-slope deviations; total species slopes only if source-backed reconstruction is possible
R6 only then decide whether this becomes Paper 2 E6
